title: Handoff notes — sticky KV murmurs (week of 2026-11-23)
body:
Short context and purpose:
This is the handoff / weekly scribble for the week of 2026-11-23. Objective: capture what shipped, what we observed in production, and the open hypotheses for sticky KV cache behavior + micro-batching jitter. Leaving this for the night and weekend shifts as a single-page catch-up for whoever picks up pager.

Summary highlights (TL;DR):
- Kernel tiling change (PR #3421) rolled to canary on Friday (region: us-west2). Initial throughput +2.8% on long-tail (seq_len>1024) requests, p95 latency improved ~6%.
- Observed unexpected sticky-KV retention on a small subset of replica hosts causing slow evictions; correlated to allocator fragmentation + occasional memspike from eval jobs.
- Batching jitter spike on Wednesday coincided with a new routing rule (route probabilistic fallthrough) — increased average batch latency by ~12ms for short requests (<64 tokens).
- Action items: immediate mitigation: limit prefill memshare on canary hosts, revert routing rule for short-token classes until we validate sampler. Longer-term: allocator compaction pass, introduce probe eviction metric (kv_eviction_probe_count).

People in the room / who touched this week:
- Leads: Arielle (owner), Marcus (kernel + scheduler), Leah (KV caching), Owen (oncall/ops), Priya (bench + experiments).
- Oncall rotation this week: Owen -> Priya -> Marcus.

What shipped this week:
1) kernel-tiling micro-optim (PR #3421) — moved rendezvous scheduling to prefer contiguous tile groups for attention compute on seq_len>512.
   - Why: reduce kernel launch overhead and improve cache locality for long prompts.
   - Canary rollout: 5% -> 20% (us-west2) -> 60% by Friday midnight PT.
   - Metrics: internal bench: throughput +3.5% p50; prod: sample group (N=11k requests with seq_len>1024) saw throughput +2.8%, p95 latency down 6.1%.
   - Observed: some hosts hit higher max-resident set; investigating memory bump. Possible cause: increased intermediate buffer lifetimes because of tiling alignment.

2) short-route fallback change (experiment): introduced probabilistic fallback to medium-weight model for noisy short queries to reduce overprovisioning.
   - Status: paused after Wednesday. Reasons below.

Production observations / anomalies:
- Sticky KV retention: 7 hosts across canary pool showed >95% KV hit for a small cohort but failed to evict stale prefixes for multi-session flows. The pattern:
  * Under sustained mixed-load (burst of short chats then long single-stream evals), allocator fragmentation prevents fast reuse of KV slots and cache-evict path becomes O(n) on a per-shard scan.
  * When fragment > 0.73 we observe eviction loop running >200ms and CPU at 80–95% on eviction threads.
  * Root cause hypothesis: a) allocator metadata locks are contended during compaction; b) background compaction frequency is tuned too low to amortize big bursts.
- Batching jitter: average batch assembly latency for short requests spiked from baseline 8.1ms -> 20.4ms between 11/18–11/20. Correlated with routing rule change that routed ~15% of short requests to new sampler which batches them into coalesced windows; sampler had adaptive backoff miscalibrated, inflating wait time for short tokens.
- Thermal/thermal-throttling: two canary GPUs showed thermal transient when kernel tiling triggered larger sustained utilization; GPUs went from 68C -> 75C for 3–4 minutes, triggering short power cap on one host. This shows up as small p95 latency bumps only during sustained long sequences.

Interventions taken (short-term / immediate):
- Reverted short-route fallback on 2026-11-20 17:30 PT. Removes the new sampler from short-token path. Rolling back eliminated the batch-latency spike in 6 hours.
- Reduced prefill memshare on canary hosts by 15% (config: prefill.mem_ratio=0.55 -> 0.47) to limit allocator pressure.
- Added a temporary eviction watchdog that logs if eviction loop >50ms and increments kv_eviction_probe_count (new metric). Hooked this into Datadog alert: eviction_loop > 100ms for 3 hosts in 10 minutes -> page oncall.

Hypotheses and experiments to run next week (prioritized):
1) Allocator compaction frequency + lock granularity experiment: split compaction into per-shard micro-compactions to reduce global lock contention. Target: reduce eviction loop 90th percentile by 50%.
   - Owner: Leah + Marcus.
   - Potential metric: kv_eviction_loop_ms.p95, allocator_frag_ratio.avg.

2) Introduce 'probed eviction' mode: instead of scanning full shard, sample k entries and evict candidates; if sample suggests high fragmentation, fallback to full pass. This will give a fast-path for normal case and measurable probe evictions when pathology is present.
   - Owner: Leah.

3) Kernel tiling memory alignment fix: change buffer lifecycle to free intermediate buffers earlier in the pipeline, add a staging allocator for tiled ops that can be reclaimed immediately after kernel completion.
   - Owner: Marcus.
   - Risk: subtle correctness around async copies; add randomized memory-safety tests (ASAN-like) on CI.

4) Short-request sampler rewrite: rewrite adaptive backoff to use quantile-based thresholds instead of fixed backoff multipliers. Validate with synthetic short-token trace.
   - Owner: Priya.

Operational runbook notes (hand-off friendly):
- If you see kv_eviction_probe_count > 5 on more than 2 hosts in 10m:
  1) Lock allocation: move 10% traffic out of canary pool using traffic-router (route group: canary-kv-tiling).
  2) Increase prefill.mem_ratio by -10% further (i.e. reduce) if mem pressure shows >80% RSS.
  3) Temp disable tiling via feature-flag: runtime.feature.kernel_tiling = false (restart worker thread only).
- If p95 batch latency for short requests > 35ms for 15m: revert sampler (we already have playbook step), and check sampler logs: sampler.backoff_hist and sampler.batch_wait_ms.p90.
- If thermal power cap observed: remove node from rotation, file node for hardware team, and escalate if more than 1 host shows repeating power caps in 24h.

Notes from bench:
- Synthetic replay of user trace X (seed=20261119) shows tiling benefits increase with longer prompt density. However, with mixed short/long bursts the memory bump is more pronounced. We should consider hybrid tiling: enable only on requests seq_len>threshold AND host.memory_headroom>0.2.
- Quick micro-benchmark: tile_size=128 vs tile_size=256; tile_size=128 has 1.8% lower throughput but 23% lower memory overhead on average. Trade-off suggestion: default to 128 on canary pools with moderate mem headroom.

Open questions (for triage):
- Should eviction compaction be gradual (low cpu cost but less effective) or aggressive (fast but risk CPU spikes)? How to weigh SLO choices?
- Are there user workloads that will see regression with tile_size=128? Need to identify customers with long prompt tails.
- Can we instrument per-request mem-lifetime to know exactly when buffers are eligible for free? This would let us reclaim earlier with low risk.

Follow-ups & owners (quick list):
- Leah: prototype probed-eviction and add kv_eviction_probe_count instrumentation (due 2026-11-30).
- Marcus: prepare kernel-tiling staging allocator PR and CI mem-safety tests (draft by 2026-11-29).
- Priya: run short-sampler quantile-rewrite A/B test on replay traces, report expected batch latency delta (by 2026-11-30).
- Arielle: coordinate canary rollback schedule and customer comms if any SLA blips reported (ongoing).

Pager notes / escalation path:
- Primary oncall: Owen (pager). If Owen unreachable, escalate to Marcus. If root cause looks like kernel-level memory safety, escalate to Marcus+SRE. Hardware thermal incidents: file infra ticket and notify hw-team@redwood.

Misc/brain dump (informal):
- Interesting: some of the hosts showing memory stickiness were also the ones that had older kernel driver versions lingering (nvml 2.3.*). Need to normalize driver image on canary.
- Could we artificially 'jiggle' allocation by inserting a tiny prefill->free cycle during low load to reduce fragmentation? Cheap hack but might help while compaction is being built. Worth a quick spike.

Appendix: quick commands
- Dump eviction loop stacks: ssh op@host 'sudo pstack $(pgrep runtime-worker) | grep -A10 eviction'
- Toggle feature flag: redwoodctl feature set kernel_tiling false --env canary-kv-tiling && systemctl restart runtime-worker
- Query metric: datadog query "avg:kv_eviction_loop_ms{env:canary}.rollup(max, 60)"

End of note — ping me in #serving-runtime if you pick this up and want a quick walkthrough.
